o: Identify the four main IDE facilities named in J277.
Explain what each does for a programmer.
Use simple IDE diagnostics and run tools to improve code.
c: The editor is where programmers write and change source code. Syntax highlighting and suggestions may make code easier to read and reduce typing mistakes.
Diagnostics report issues in code, such as missing brackets or incorrect syntax. A programmer can use the message and line number to find and correct the error.
The IDE provides a way to run and test the program and inspect the output. This helps programmers check whether the program behaves as expected.
A compiler or interpreter provided within an IDE converts source code into executable instructions. Together, editor, diagnostics, translator and running tools support the development cycle.

m.title: Model an IDE debugging explanation
m.q: A program's running total is incorrect. Explain how a breakpoint and a watch can help locate the error. [4 marks]
st: In the editor, identify where the total is updated; a breakpoint can be placed just before that line.
The breakpoint pauses execution [1], so the programmer can investigate the calculation [1].
A watch displays the current value of total [1] while stepping through the program.
The programmer can compare values before and after each change and find where the incorrect result first appears [1].

w: Explain how an editor's syntax highlighting and auto-completion can help a programmer. [4 marks]
Syntax highlighting makes different code elements easier to distinguish [1], making code easier to read [1]. Auto-completion suggests names or commands [1], which can reduce typing errors [1].
Describe the purpose of the run-time environment and translator provided by an IDE. [4 marks]

The run-time environment allows a program to be executed and tested [1], letting the programmer inspect behaviour and output [1]. A translator converts source code into a form the CPU can execute [1], enabling the program to run [1].
An IDE reports 'missing closing bracket' at line 2. Explain how diagnostics and the editor help fix the problem. [4 marks]
Diagnostics identify the possible issue [1] and help locate the line [1]. The editor lets the programmer change the code [1], after which they can run or test it again to check the correction [1].

wSteps: Identify one editor feature at a time.
What does colouring code help you notice?
Why do suggestions help reduce mistakes?
Highlights code elements [1] for readability [1]; suggestions [1] reduce mistyping [1].
Which facility makes code executable? Which runs it?
Explain execution and observation of output.
Translator converts [1] for CPU [1]; run-time executes/tests [1] to inspect results [1].
Read the message and locate its line.
Use the editor to insert the missing bracket.
Run the updated source to test the correction.
Diagnostic message [1] and location [1]; editor correction [1] and retest [1].

k.q: Predict the output. A learner expected 7 — is this code correct?
k.code:
total = 5
total = total + 2
total = total + 2
print(total)
p: Find the line that causes the unexpected result.
Edit the source so it prints 7.
Run the changed program again and check your prediction.
k.a: Original output 9. Remove the second addition on line 3 to print 7; retest.

e:
A pupil writes a program in an IDE. Describe how an editor and error diagnostics help the pupil. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style practice question.
The editor allows entry and correction of source code [1] so mistakes can be fixed [1]. Diagnostics report errors [1] and help the pupil locate the faulty code [1].

Explain how a run-time environment and a translator within an IDE are used while developing a program. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style practice question.

The translator converts source code into instructions suitable for execution [1], enabling the program to run [1]. The run-time environment executes or tests the program [1], allowing output and behaviour to be checked [1].

A learner's program should print 7 but prints 9. Suggest TWO distinct IDE actions to locate and correct the error. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style practice question.
Use the IDE's editor to inspect and correct the repeated calculation [1] and save the corrected source [1]. Run the corrected code in the IDE [1] and verify that its output is now 7 [1].
v: Integrated Development Environment: software bringing programming tools together.
Tool used to write and modify source code.
A message that helps identify an error and often its location.
Facility for executing and testing a program.
Tool that turns source code into executable instructions.
A point where a debugger can pause a running program for inspection.
x: An IDE's run-time environment helps a programmer execute and test code.
r: When does a compiler normally translate the source program? [1 mark]
Before execution, translating the whole source program [1].
State ONE advantage of a high-level language for school application development. [1 mark]
Easier to read, maintain or port [1].
For a three-input AND gate, state the output when its inputs are 1,1,0. [1 mark]
0 [1]; all three must be 1 for AND to give 1.
A program changes frequently and must give quick error feedback while testing. Explain why an interpreter may suit this development task. [3 marks]
It executes code during interpretation [1], allowing immediate testing [1] and identifying errors when the relevant statement is reached [1].
